subject.title: Feature/Fix: Validate and optimize lineage token accounting

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage-accounting architecture, and if so should the overlapping identity/cache work from https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118 be incorporated into it or landed separately first?
rationale: Both approaches improve the same fork-accounting area, but one is a broad reversible architecture and the other a narrow production fix; tests cannot determine the desired permanent scanner design or maintenance cost.

options.title: Sponsor and reconcile the lineage stack
options.body: Review the four PRs in dependency order, fold in or explicitly supersede overlapping identity/cache behavior, and keep lineage authority gated behind further validation.

options.title: Land the narrow fix first
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118 for the immediate production defect and pause this architecture until remaining accounting gaps justify its complexity.

options.title: Keep both experimental temporarily
options.body: Land only non-authoritative seams after proving they do not duplicate production behavior, then make a later promotion decision from broader corpus evidence.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and reconcile the lineage stack
recommendation.body: Review the four PRs in dependency order, fold in or explicitly supersede overlapping identity/cache behavior, and keep lineage authority gated behind further validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice sets the repository's long-term scanner architecture and determines how two overlapping contributor implementations should be reconciled.
